0.heading: Overview
refs: Luke 13:1 , Christ preaches repentance upon the punishment of the Galilaeans and others
Luke 13:6 , The fruitless fig-tree may not stand
Luke 13:10 , He heals the crooked woman
Luke 13:18 , shows the powerful working of the word in the hearts of his chosen, by the parable of the grain of mustard seed, and of leaven
Luke 13:22 , exhorts to enter in at the strait gate
Luke 13:31 , and reproves Herod and Jerusalem.

1.heading: the Galilaeans:
refs: The Galilaeans are frequently mentioned by Josephus as the most turbulent and seditious people, being upon all occasions ready to disturb the Roman authority. It is uncertain to what event our Lord refers

but is probable that they were the followers of Judas Gaulonitis, who opposed paying tribute to Caesar and submitting to the Roman government. A party of them coming to Jerusalem during one of the great festivals, and presenting their oblations in the court of the temple, Pilate treacherously sent a company of soldiers, who slew them, and "mingled their blood with their sacrifices." Acts 5:37
